About the model & sky data
The Sun and Earth are enlarged; the celestial sphere is a map of directions, not stellar distances. Earth’s orbit is shown as a circle; the solar position includes the main effect of eccentricity. Stars are precessed to 2026.5; proper motion, refraction and parallax are omitted. Constellation lines are traditional guides, not IAU boundaries.

Stars: HYG v4.1, David Nash (CC BY-SA 4.0). Sky figures: d3-celestial, Olaf Frohn (BSD-3-Clause). Data & licences.

Solar model: US Naval Observatory. Renderer: Three.js (MIT). All rendering libraries and sky data are included with this site.

# Sky data for Ecliptic Explorer

## Stars

`stars.json` contains 8,920 real stars from HYG v4.1 with apparent visual magnitude V <= 6.5, excluding the Sun. HYG v4.1 is a pinned release, not the latest HYG release. The source CSV was downloaded from:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/astronexus/HYG-Database/main/hyg/CURRENT/hygdata_v41.csv

Source project: https://github.com/astronexus/HYG-Database
Creator/project: David Nash / Astronomy Nexus, https://www.astronexus.com/projects/hyg
License: Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/
The adapted `stars.json` is also licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Retain this attribution and license link when distributing it.

Changes: selected only stars V <= 6.5; excluded Sol; kept HYG/Hipparcos IDs, names/designations, J2000 right ascension and declination, V magnitude, B-V colour index and constellation; rounded coordinates to six decimals; sorted by magnitude and converted CSV to JSON. No artificial stars were added.

Each star is an object:
`{id, hip, name, ra, dec, mag, bv, con}`

- `id`: numeric HYG ID
- `hip`: numeric Hipparcos ID, or null
- `name`: proper name, else Bayer/Flamsteed designation, else HIP/HYG ID label
- `ra`: J2000 right ascension in HOURS, range [0,24)
- `dec`: J2000 declination in DEGREES
- `mag`: apparent visual magnitude
- `bv`: B-V colour index, or null
- `con`: IAU three-letter constellation identifier

J2000 positions are retained. Proper motion, precession, nutation, aberration and atmospheric refraction are not applied by this data adaptation. The application should disclose its educational approximation or transform these coordinates if required. B-V may be mapped to an approximate colour; do not imply exact rendered photometry.

## Constellations

`constellations-compact.json` contains 89 records (Serpens has two components), including all 13 constellations traversed by the ecliptic. Derived from Olaf Frohn's d3-celestial data:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ofrohn/d3-celestial/master/data/constellations.lines.json
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ofrohn/d3-celestial/master/data/constellations.json
Project: https://github.com/ofrohn/d3-celestial
Copyright (c) 2015 Olaf Frohn. BSD-3-Clause. Retain `d3-license.txt` with distributed data.

The project credits IAU constellation charts and modifications by Olaf Frohn. These are conventional constellation stick figures, not formal IAU boundaries. Do not call their lines boundaries.

Each record:
`{id,name,ra,dec,rank,lines}`

- label `ra` is hours, `dec` degrees (J2000)
- `lines` is an array of polylines; each polyline is `[[raHours,decDegrees], ...]`
- convert every adjacent pair into a line segment; do NOT connect different polylines
- `rank` is the source's visual prominence rank (1 most prominent)

Changes: selected Latin names, label coordinates and rank; removed translated names; normalised right ascension to [0,24) hours; converted equatorial degrees to hours; compacted JSON.
